headline: KSE-100 extends its rebound for a third straight session even as the US-Iran Hormuz conflict keeps escalating on the wire -- a genuine domestic buy-the-dip, but not yet an all-clear.
summary: PSX has rallied for three sessions straight, clawing back most of last week's Hormuz-driven crash on value-buying, even though the US and Iran are still trading strikes and the naval blockade remains active -- Brent crude sits near $86 and the desk's georisk gauge just ticked up to 59/moderate. Domestically the backdrop stays solid: SBP holds at 11.5%, June CPI eased to 11.1%, reserves rose to $18.47bn, and the next MPC is July 27. The desk reads this as a genuine but fragile bounce -- constructive on banks, fertiliser and E&P where the macro logic is real, cautious on OMCs, autos and textile-exporters exposed to the fuel and freight side of the same shock.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: SBP is holding the policy rate at 11.5% into the July 27 MPC while T-bill cutoffs have settled 30-40bps below it, a spread that supports bank net interest margins.

sectors.name: Fertilizer
sectors.why: Domestic-demand defensive with low direct oil-import exposure -- insulated from the Hormuz-driven crude spike that's hitting importers elsewhere.

sectors.name: E&P (oil & gas exploration)
sectors.why: Direct beneficiary of Brent holding near $86 while the naval blockade and fresh US strikes keep a floor under crude prices.

sectors.name: OMCs
sectors.why: Weekly-repriced fuel costs and circular-debt risk, with the next petroleum price review (2026-07-17) more likely a hike or flat roll than a cut while Brent stays elevated.

sectors.name: Autos
sectors.why: Imported-input costs and softer consumer demand under fuel/inflation pressure -- June passenger-car sales were down 12.9% YoY even as FY26 headline volumes rose.

sectors.name: Textiles / exporters
sectors.why: Gulf freight-cost exposure from the active naval blockade, and FY26 exports already stagnant at $17.93bn with June down 16.71% YoY.

sectors.name: Cement
sectors.why: Rallied hard today on broad value-buying, but imported-fuel/coal costs cut the other way against a still-strong domestic construction cycle -- a genuine two-way name, not a clean call either direction.

watchlist.angle: DCR just declared its final FY26 dividend (news impact 4, filed 2026-07-15) with a confirmed book closure on 2026-07-25 (buy-by 2026-07-22, Rs0.66/unit, 1.72% yield) -- it's also the single most predictable name on the desk's whole board right now (predictability score 75.7, top of the universe) and sits just 1.6% off its 20-day high, with two proven breakout strategies on file: donchian55_break (71.4% hit rate over 21 trades) and high52w_break (72.7% hit rate over 11 trades).
watchlist.risk: Fundamentals flag the payout as stretched -- DCR is paying out 112% of earnings, so a soft rental-income year could force a dividend cut despite the fresh declaration.

watchlist.angle: Banks are the macro's favoured sector into a still-hawkish 11.5% policy rate, and UBL's own back-test shows its consolidation-break setup (donch20_pullback_break) hitting 76.3% over 38 trades, still 80% out-of-sample -- fundamentals screen attractive (P/E 8.14, 6.92% yield covered by just 56% of profit), with results due 2026-07-22.
watchlist.risk: That results date is only a scraped estimate, unconfirmed -- a delay or a soft print would remove the near-term catalyst without warning.

watchlist.angle: NBP is one of the desk's top-10 most predictable names (score 62.3) and screens attractive on fundamentals -- cheapest P/E among the banks (5.48) alongside a 17.14% dividend yield that eats only 22% of profit -- with a proven consolidation-break strategy (63% hit rate over 27 trades) and today's +2.25% move keeping it above both its 20- and 50-day averages.
watchlist.risk: NBP's beta of 1.14 means it moves harder than the market both ways -- in a regime the desk still calls only 'moderate' risk, a re-escalation would likely hit NBP faster than its lower-beta bank peers.

watchlist.angle: Fertiliser is macro-favoured (domestic demand, low oil-import beta), FFC is a top-10 predictable name (score 66.5), and its 52-week-high breakout is the strongest edge in its own back-test file -- 77.8% hit rate over 27 trades, still 71.4% out-of-sample -- with results due 2026-07-29.
watchlist.risk: FFC is currently trading below both its 20- and 50-day averages (RSI 45.9) -- the breakout thesis needs the stock to actually reclaim those levels first; it isn't triggering today.

watchlist.angle: ENGROH is cheap on fundamentals (P/E 5.12, cheapest third of PSX) in the macro-favoured fertiliser space, has a live oscillator trigger today (Williams %R mid cross) plus a stronger proven edge on file (stochastic-reclaim-50: 76.9% hit rate over 13 trades), and jumped +3.39% today on renewed buying.
watchlist.risk: ENGROH pays no dividend, so the entire thesis rests on price appreciation -- there's no income cushion if the rally stalls.

catalysts.event: Weekly petroleum price review -- Brent still near $86 makes a further hike or flat roll more likely than a cut
UBL results (scraped estimate, unconfirmed) and DCR dividend buy-by deadline
DCR book closure begins (confirmed, final FY26 dividend Rs0.66/unit)
SBP MPC -- first monetary policy decision of FY27; DCR book closure ends same day

risks: The Hormuz conflict is not de-escalating on the ground -- fresh US strikes on Iranian territory, a disabled tanker, Iran refusing talks, and an active naval blockade all continued this week even as PSX rallied; a two-session equity bounce against an intensifying conflict is a divergence to respect, not a confirmed all-clear.

Brent crude near $86 keeps the next fuel-price review (2026-07-17) tilted toward another hike, which would squeeze OMCs, autos and textile-exporters further and feed through to broader inflation and PKR pressure.

The desk's georisk score ticked up to 59/moderate (from 55) with the conflict-escalation factor pinned at its maximum reading of 100 -- the radar has not confirmed any real de-escalation even though the tape looks calm.
